newsitem.title: LATVIA: STOCK PRICES UP, FUNDS SEEN BACK.
newsitem.headline: STOCK PRICES UP, FUNDS SEEN BACK.

text.p: Latvian stock prices mostly advanced on Wednesday and funds were seen slowly returning to the bourse as voucher prices have reached unattractive highs, dealers said.
Total turnover fell to 63,000 lats from 125,000 lats.
The Rietumu index added 2.98 percent to 181.26 and the Saule10 closed at 141.16, up 3.21 percent.

"Dealers were mostly smiling today as funds were seen coming back to the speculative market from the rival voucher market," Aldis Sipols, securities department head of the Savings Bank (Krajbanka), told Reuters.
"The current price of 2.70 lats a voucher is too expensive for those wanting to exchange them for shares and nothing much in terms of big privatisation is expected during the summer," he said.
Riga Shipyard was the most traded stock on volume of 17,500 lats and it rose to 1.35 lats from 1.32 lats.
All official list stocks gained ground and the Riga Transport Fleet saw 9,100 lats of shares traded and it added two santimes to 1.28 lats.
Unibanka jumped to 3.16 lats from 3.01 lats on trade of 3,200 lats while Staburadze had volume of 3,700 lats.
It advanced three santimes to 2.53 lats.
A smaller stock, Strenchi Forestry, dominated the secondary list on good first quarter results.
It registered trade of 11,500 lats and jumped to 1.43 lats or 14 percent, adding 18 santimes.
Strenchi earlier reported a first quarter profit of 130,878 lats.
Meanwhile Talsi Forestry, which also posted a similar first quarter result of 123,229 lats profit, saw slow trade.
"I would expect a rise in Talsi as both forestry companies are comparable in value while Talsi's price is much cheaper," Savings Bank's Sipols said.
Talsi had a tiny volume of 400 lats as it rose to 0.48 lats from 0.42 lats.
Elsewhere on the secondary market Valmiera Glassfibre registered trade of 6,100 and it closed up at 1.46 lats against 1.42 lats while Daugavpils Chain traded 5,300 lats.
It edged up one santime to 2.31 lats.
